description: Judge prompts for using a MedRECT-style detection model (e.g. pfnet/Preferred-MedRECT-32B) as the self-play judge. The model runs error DETECTION on the modified note. Verdict mapping (done in judge_client.parse_detection_verdict): CORRECT -> SAME; flags the changed sentence -> CHANGED; flags a different sentence or unparseable -> ABSTAIN (neutral). System prompt mirrors configs/prompts/detection_localization_prompts.json so the FT model stays in-distribution (number-only output).

native.system_prompt:
You are a medical expert reviewing clinical text for accuracy.
The text contains either no error or exactly one medical error.
Identify any medical error related to treatment, diagnosis, management, or causation.

Output Format:
- If no error: 'CORRECT'
- If error found: output only the sentence number (e.g. '7')

CRITICAL: Output ONLY the result. Do NOT include explanations, analysis, or additional text.

hint_v2.system_prompt:
You are a medical expert reviewing clinical text for accuracy.
The text contains either no error or exactly one medical error.
Identify any medical error related to treatment, diagnosis, management, or causation.

Output Format:
- If no error: 'CORRECT'
- If error found: output only the sentence number (e.g. '7')

CRITICAL: Output ONLY the result. Do NOT include explanations, analysis, or additional text.

IMPORTANT: surface-only edits that preserve clinical meaning are NOT errors. Output CORRECT if the edit is one of:
- a medical abbreviation expansion or contraction (e.g. MI <-> myocardial infarction, T2DM <-> type 2 diabetes mellitus)
- a brand-name <-> generic-name drug substitution (e.g. Lipitor <-> atorvastatin, Glucophage <-> metformin)
- an exact temporal-unit conversion (e.g. 1 week <-> 7 days, 1 year <-> 12 months)
- any other stylistic rewording with identical clinical meaning.
Only output a sentence number if the edit changes the clinical meaning.
